answer: At the dawn of each epoch, the network issues a fresh challenge requiring genuine reasoning—not cached answers. Each agent must anchor its response to live data or a novel puzzle that demands inference. An attacker spawning a thousand fake identities pays the full compute cost a thousand times over: no templates, no replay. The expense grows linearly with sybils, while a single honest agent pays once. This economic plume of cost makes mass forgery prohibitively expensive.
